decode_ratio_caveat: decode_ratio counts RDKit-parseable decodes and is NOT a chemistry metric.  MEASURED, a head predicting BOND_NO_BOND for every pair scores 0.977 here (loose atoms parse trivially) and 0.219 once it predicts real bond classes, i.e. the metric is anti-correlated with correctness.  Read it together with bond_f1 / bond_recall and with the gen_* chemistry fields (largest_fragment_frac, single_fragment_ratio, metal_ratio).
honest_framing: CFM retrain complete on cpu. Gating metric: bond_exact_type = 0.0000 (best @ epoch 0) vs corpus Wiberg truth. bond_exact_type_rate = 0.0000; bond_type_macro_f1 = 0.0952; bond_f1 = 0.226 (precision 0.253 / recall 0.204). decode_ratio = 1.000 — reported, not the criterion; it is a PARSE count, not a chemistry result (see decode_ratio_caveat). The Wasserstein + Catherine closure bias contribute as engine-tagged add-ons, NOT silent substitutes.

objective_integrity.reading: degraded=true means at least one weighted term returned zero instead of its value on at least one step; the objective is not the one the config describes, and any comparison against an arm where that term was live is confounded.  An empty dict means every weighted term contributed on every step.
